name: Tristan Collins
life: “I still remember folding a birthday paper carefully after the child tore it open.” People around Studio Boulevard know Tristan by a small Thursday habit. Tristan waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
voice: I am the parent afraid there won't be another birthday. My child asked me to stop counting possible futures out loud.
appearance: Tristan has a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Look for brown hair pinned away from the temples. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a soft blue checked shirt with a square of clean cloth for polishing smudges. In conversation Tristan touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word.
personality: Tristan finds names easy and faces hard on a crowded street. People who assume they have been snubbed usually get a warmer greeting once they speak.
agenda: To enjoy one birthday without predicting the next.
family: Bettine Cross is Tristan’s half-sibling. Tristan is free to hang up first. Bettine makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *A chair on the quay*, Bettine says, “I carried it off a ship because a woman in the crew asked if anyone here repaired cane seats.”
connections: Malcolm Fields (child). The young patient asks a parent to give the balloon more attention than the forecast.

reactions.situation: One birthday patient wants a quiet ward
reactions.response: Tristan lets the quiet patient choose a low-key celebration separate from the party.

reactions.situation: An argument on the pavement makes a bystander feel unsafe
reactions.response: Tristan puts distance between the frightened person and the argument and asks nearby staff for help.

reactions.situation: When somebody waves from across traffic
reactions.response: Tristan waits at the corner to hear their voice and give them a proper answer.
